metaHome.title: LUMINA — Many ways to explore your inner world
metaHome.description: Explore different parts of yourself through Saju, astrology, tarot, numerology, Big Five, and daily readings. Calculations, symbolism, and psychometric evidence are kept distinct.
metaHome.ogDescription: Begin with Saju, tarot, personality, or a daily reading — no sign-up required.

common.disclaimerCultural: This interpretation is self-reflection content based on traditional symbolic systems, not a scientifically verified prediction. The calculations themselves follow fixed rules — solar terms, planetary positions, shuffle algorithms, and other method-specific logic — but the claim that the results predict life events has not been empirically confirmed.
common.disclaimerEntertainment: This content is entertainment drawn from a fixed bank of phrases, varied by date and zodiac sign or animal. It isn't based on actual planetary positions or personal data, and it isn't a prediction.
common.disclaimerScientific: IPIP-50 is a personality trait scale made publicly available for academic research. It's meant to support self-understanding, not to replace medical diagnosis or clinical assessment.

errors.errorBody: Reload the page or return to the home screen.
errors.notFoundBody: Check the address or return to the home screen.

home.momentLabel: The Saju of this exact moment
home.platformBody: Use precise calculation, symbolic systems, and psychometrics to examine the self you are becoming. The ways you can explore will continue to grow — begin where curiosity leads.
home.heroBody: Solar terms are calculated directly from the sun's ecliptic longitude, not from a lookup table. True solar time is corrected using birthplace longitude and the equation of time, and historical standard-time changes — like Korea's UTC+8:30 in 1954 or daylight saving in 1988 — are factored in as they occurred. There's no sign-up, and anything you enter stays only in this browser.
home.hubHeading: Which part of yourself would you like to meet today?
home.hubIntro: Trace the shape of a birth moment, sit with a question, notice repeated tendencies, or check the rhythm of today. LUMINA's methods of self-exploration will keep expanding.
home.hubSajuDesc: Calculate your birth chart, elements, and life cycles from your exact birth date and time.
home.hubTarotDesc: Choose a spread and draw cards for this moment.
home.hubNumerologyDesc: Read tendencies in the numbers of your birth date.
home.hubPsychometricsDesc: Answer 50 questions to see five personality traits.
home.hubJungianDesc: Read IPIP-50 responses on four axes and summarize them as one of 16 MBTI types.
home.hubDarkTriadDesc: Measure Machiavellianism, Narcissism, and Psychopathy traits.
home.hubAttachmentDesc: Analyze patterns in intimate relationships along anxiety and avoidance dimensions.
home.hubHoroscopeDesc: Check today's tone by zodiac sign or animal.
home.hubCompatibilityDesc: Compare traditional Saju relationship signals side by side.
home.mandalaHeading: Paths into your inner world move around the present moment.
home.mandalaBody: At the center is the Saju of now. The surrounding nodes are the ways you can begin exploring yourself today. Grounded in the actual sky, this map lets different methods lead back to the same inner landscape.
home.mandalaStageLabel: A mandala of today's sky and self-exploration
home.mandalaLegend: Initial node positions use geocentric ecliptic longitude of date; motion follows each body's daily movement. R means retrograde.
home.hubFormPrompt: Choose the “Saju” card above to open the input form here.
home.nowBody: Today's day pillar, true solar time, lunar phase, and Mercury's movement become one compact record. The source of each calculation stays visible.
home.nowEvidence: Basis: the day pillar comes from solar-term and stem-branch calculation; lunar and planetary data come from astronomical positions.
home.trustHeading: Fun and evidence share the same screen.
home.trustBody: LUMINA never blends every result into one kind of truth. Badges distinguish scientific measurement, cultural symbolism, and entertainment so you can choose how to read each result.
home.trustScientificBody: Results such as Big Five follow public scales and psychometric principles. We show continuous scores and the limits of measurement together.
home.trustCulturalBody: Saju, tarot, and astrology offer long-lived symbolic systems as paths for reflection. Read them as reflection, not prediction.
home.trustEntertainmentBody: Daily horoscope content is designed to be light and enjoyable. Its entertainment purpose stays explicit.
home.reportHeading: Each method leaves a result in its own language.
home.reportIntro: Instead of making every page feel like Saju, this overview shows what each feature calculates and what kind of question it opens.

saju.newIntro: Enter your birth information to calculate it in this browser, with no sign-up.
saju.emptyBody: No birth info has been entered yet.
saju.brokenLink: This link's result couldn't be read.
saju.cannotCompute: A Saju chart can't be calculated from this value.
saju.dayMasterNote: The Day Master is {hanja} {ko} ({element}). Every other character is read against this one — Ten Gods and Growth Stages both come from here.
saju.pillarFootnote: The bottom row lists, top to bottom: Hidden Stems (Residual · Middle · Principal), Growth Stage, and Zodiac Animal. Void is {void}. The depth each pillar stands at reflects how much weight it carries in interpretation.
saju.tenGodsAside: Relative to the Day Master · eight characters
saju.calcNote: The Year and Month Pillars are set by solar terms, the Day Pillar by the Julian day number, and the Hour Pillar by true solar time. The lunar calendar isn't used in the calculation — it's shown only for reference.
saju.seasonalHint: Whether the Month Branch supports the Day Master
saju.rootHint: Whether the Day Branch supports the Day Master
saju.peerHint: Whether the remaining characters support the Day Master
saju.strengthNoteStrong: Energy that supports the Day Master dominates. Drawing it down looks closer to balance.
saju.strengthNoteBalanced: Supporting and draining energy are close to even. This doesn't lean firmly either way.
saju.strengthNoteWeak: Energy that drains the Day Master dominates. Adding to it looks closer to balance.
saju.strengthFootnote: Schools of thought differ on how to judge this, so here it rests only on the weighted Five Elements ratio and Seasonal/Root/Broad Support.
saju.tenGodsFootnote: The five groups are split by their Five Elements relationship to the Day Master — which is why their colors match the Five Elements distribution. Branch Ten Gods are judged by the Hidden Stem's Principal Qi, since Zi, Wu, Si, and Hai have a mismatch between their positional and essential polarity.
saju.luckDirectionNote: {direction} · first Major Luck period starts at age {age} ({note})
saju.tenGodGroupSelfGloss: Power like your own — peers and rivals
saju.tenGodGroupOutputGloss: Power you put out — expression and output
saju.tenGodGroupWealthGloss: Power you manage — wealth and results
saju.tenGodGroupOfficerGloss: Power that presses on you — discipline and status
saju.tenGodGroupResourceGloss: Power that helps you — learning and protection
saju.tenGodGuideTitle: A guide to the Ten Gods
saju.tenGodGuideBody: The Ten Gods translate the Five-Element and polarity relationship between the Day Master and another character into traditional role language. These lines do not determine personality or events; they offer a direction for reflection.
saju.tenGodDictionaryTitle: Open the complete Ten Gods dictionary
saju.tenGodDictionaryNote: This is the full dictionary, including relationships that are not shown in the current chart. Ten Gods present in the chart are shown first above.
saju.interpretationLuckNote: Open each period to see its calculated interval and traditional symbolism. These are prompts for reviewing choices and conditions, not predictions of events.
saju.rarityTitle: Distinctiveness of the visible element signature
saju.rarityBody: This is not a population frequency or fortune probability. It counts how often the visible element-count signature appears when 60 sexagenary pillars receive equal symbolic weight.

tenGodReadings.friend: A relationship that shares the same kind of force as the self. Notice the standards you protect when collaborating or competing.
tenGodReadings.robWealth: A relationship in which speed and priorities may differ around shared resources. Reflect on the balance between sharing and boundaries.
tenGodReadings.eatingGod: A relationship that sends thought and energy outward. Notice how you make, express, and care for something steadily.
tenGodReadings.hurtingOfficer: A relationship that looks at existing rules from another angle. Consider the balance between honest expression and relational adjustment.
tenGodReadings.indirectWealth: A relationship with changing resources and opportunities. Set a clear anchor so flexibility does not become scattered effort.
tenGodReadings.directWealth: A relationship with recurring responsibility and practical resources. Check the routines and promises you can sustain over time.
tenGodReadings.sevenKillings: A relationship with pressure and challenge. Consider whether tension can become training and a clearer boundary.
tenGodReadings.directOfficer: A relationship with rules, responsibility, and public standards. Notice where outside expectations meet your own principles.
tenGodReadings.indirectResource: A relationship with learning and recovery outside familiar frames. Notice the time you need to digest things privately and find a new angle.
tenGodReadings.directResource: A relationship with learning, protection, and received support. Reflect on how you accept help and build inner ground.

stageReadings.growth: A cycle in which new energy begins to take root. Notice what you want to cultivate rather than rushing the first step.
stageReadings.bath: A cycle of changing the visible form. Consider whether the way you present yourself still matches what you need.
stageReadings.cap: A cycle of taking on role and responsibility. Think about how you will share what you have prepared with the wider world.
stageReadings.prosperity: A cycle of standing on your own and repeating what works. Notice the difference between self-reliance and rigidity.
stageReadings.peak: A cycle of greater force and visibility. Alongside expansion, consider where restraint and generosity are needed.
stageReadings.decline: A cycle of adjusting a peak approach and handing something forward. Sort what to release from what to keep.
stageReadings.illness: A cycle that invites slower pace, recovery, and care. This traditional label does not mean a health event.
stageReadings.death: A cycle in which one form closes and a transition is prepared. This traditional label does not predict literal death or misfortune.
stageReadings.tomb: A cycle of storing and digesting experience. Notice what needs time to become your own before it is shared.
stageReadings.extinction: A cycle of ending an old connection and setting a new standard. Consider what must be cleared for the next choice to become visible.
stageReadings.gestation: A cycle of holding a possibility that is not visible yet. Care for the conditions rather than forcing an outcome.
stageReadings.nurture: A cycle of protecting and growing a small possibility. Notice the environment and support that make continuity possible.

saju.stageNote: The Twelve Stages are traditional metaphors for the relationship between the Day Master and a branch. Labels such as Illness and Death are not health or lifespan predictions.
saju.luckTransitionNote: Major Luck converts the distance between birth and a solar-term boundary at three days per year, then displays ten-year periods. Boundary readings vary across schools and conversion methods.
saju.yearlyInterpretation: Annual Luck shows the year's stem-branch relationship with the Day Master through the Ten Gods and Twelve Stages. It is a cultural reference, not an event calendar.
saju.noteTimeUnknown: No birth time was entered, so the Hour Pillar wasn't set. The Year, Month, and Day Pillars remain accurate.
saju.noteLateZiHour: This birth falls in the 23:00 hour. The Day Pillar was set using the theory that the day changes at 23:00 — under the midnight theory, the Day Pillar would shift one day earlier.
saju.noteTrueSolarShift: By the clock this falls in the {clockName} Hour ({clockHanja}), but true solar time — corrected for longitude and the equation of time — places it in the {solarName} Hour ({solarHanja}). The Hour Pillar follows the corrected time.
saju.noteNearTermBoundary: This is {hours} hours from the solar term boundary. A slightly different birth time would change the Month Pillar.
saju.noteGenderUnspecified: Gender wasn't entered, so Major Luck was set to run forward. Adding gender determines the actual direction.
saju.noteDST: Daylight saving time was in effect when you were born. The calculation subtracts one hour from the clock time.
saju.dialAriaLabel: Solar term dial. The birth time falls {days} days after the {term} entry point.
saju.dialDaysSince: Born {days} days after the term entry
saju.missingSuffix: directly, though it may still show up in the weighted total through Hidden Stems.
saju.allPresentNote: All five elements appear among the eight characters.
saju.wheelAriaLabel: Five Elements generating and controlling wheel. The strongest energy is {element}.
saju.wheelLegendDayMaster: The node with a dashed halo is the Day Master

astro.balanceNote: This counts which element and modality the 10 planets cluster in. Color isn't used here because astrology's four classical elements are a different system from Saju's Five Elements — using the same colors would make the two look equivalent.
astro.planetsAside: Ecliptic longitude · true equinox of date
astro.aspectsNote: An aspect forms when two planets' angular separation falls within orb of a defined angle. Aspects involving the Sun or Moon use a 2° wider orb — this varies by school of thought, so it's exposed as an option.
astro.calcNote: Planetary positions are geocentric apparent ecliptic longitudes, set to the tropical zodiac with that moment's equinox (true equinox of date) as 0°. Aberration and light-time are accounted for.
astro.wheelCaption1: Ascendant on the left · ecliptic longitude counterclockwise
astro.housePickerNote: The house system changes the spatial partition used to read the same planetary positions. Placidus may fall back to Equal near polar latitudes.
astro.metaDescription: {birthLabel} birth chart — planetary positions calculated astronomically.
astro.brokenLink: This link's result couldn't be read.
astro.wheelAriaLabel: Birth chart wheel. The Ascendant sits on the left and ecliptic longitude increases counterclockwise.
astro.noteTimeUnknown: No birth time was entered, so the Ascendant, Midheaven, and houses weren't set. Earth rotates 1° every 4 minutes, so these can't be determined without a time.
astro.noteMoonSignAmbiguous: The Moon moves about 13° per day. Since the time is unknown, noon was used as the reference point — and this position is close to a sign boundary, so the actual sign could be the neighboring one.
astro.notePolarLatitude: This birth falls within the polar circle. At this latitude there are times when the Ascendant isn't defined, so the value may be unstable.
astro.noteDst: Daylight saving time was in effect when you were born. The calculation subtracts one hour from the clock time.
astro.noteHouseSystem: Houses are calculated with the selected Whole Sign, Equal, or Placidus system.
astro.noteHouseFallback: The birth latitude is near the polar circle, where Placidus is difficult to define reliably, so the chart fell back to Equal houses.
astro.interpretationNote: Planets describe what to notice, while signs describe a traditional symbolic style for expressing it. These combinations do not fix a temperament or predict events; they are prompts for self-observation.
astro.placementFormat: {planet} in {sign} invites reflection on “{theme}” through a {mode} style.

aspectReadings.conjunction: A symbolic conjunction in which two functions gather at one point. Notice how to coordinate them without letting one erase the other.
aspectReadings.sextile: An aspect that suggests room for cooperation. A small experiment can show how the connection works in practice.
aspectReadings.square: An aspect that exposes friction between two functions. Treat it as a place for adjustment rather than a defect.
aspectReadings.trine: An aspect that can feel like an easy flow between two functions. Use the familiarity consciously instead of letting it become automatic.
aspectReadings.opposition: An aspect in which two functions face each other. Try naming both needs instead of removing one side.

tarot.heroBody: The shuffle is set by a seed generated the moment you draw. That seed rides along in the result address, so opening the same link again always shows the same cards in the same positions — nothing is stored on a server.
tarot.spreadCelticDesc: Ten cards, for a wider view of the situation
tarot.brokenLink: This link's result couldn't be read.

tarot.resultMetaDescription: LUMINA Tarot {spread} — this link always shows the same cards.
tarot.readingSingle: Right now, this position carries a sense of {keyword}.
tarot.readingWithExtra: Right now, this position also carries a sense of {first}, together with {rest}.
tarot.revealHint: Choose a position first, then meet the symbol of this moment. The result is already fixed in the link.

numerology.heroBody: The digits of your birth date are added together and reduced to a single digit. 11, 22, and 33 are kept as Master Numbers instead of being reduced further. Add a name in Roman letters to get a Destiny Number from its letter values too.
numerology.nameNote: The Destiny Number is calculated from Roman-letter values. If your name is in Korean, enter its romanized spelling instead. Leave this blank to see only the Life Path Number.
numerology.yearRangeError: You can enter a birth year between 1900 and 2100.
numerology.ignoredNote: {n} character(s) in the name weren't Roman letters and were left out of the calculation.
numerology.noDestinyNote: Add a name in Roman letters to see a Destiny Number as well.
numerology.noDestinyCta: Add a name and try again
numerology.brokenLink: The birth date couldn't be read.
numerology.invalidName: This name has no Roman letters. Please enter it using Roman letters instead.
numerology.metaDescription: Enter a birth date to get a Life Path Number, and add a Roman-letter name to get a Destiny Number too.
numerology.letterTableNote: Destiny uses the A–Z values below to sum a Roman-letter name. The letters and values used by this input are shown alongside the table.
numerology.solarOnlyNote: Numerology currently supports solar birth dates only. For a lunar profile, confirm the corresponding solar date before calculating.

psychometrics.metaDescription: A Big Five five-factor personality test built from the public-domain IPIP-50 items.
psychometrics.resultMetaDescription: Your IPIP-50 Big Five five-factor personality test result.
psychometrics.heroBody: These questions are the public-domain items released by the International Personality Item Pool. Responses aren't stored on a server — they live only in the result address — and it takes about 5–7 minutes.
psychometrics.scaleNote: The dot is the raw-score position on this scale (0–100); the band is the 95% reference interval based on measurement error. The percentile and T-score compare this response pattern with an English-language public reference sample — not a Korean norm or a diagnosis.
psychometrics.reliabilityNote: Reliability alpha is the factor-level internal-consistency value published in the official IPIP table. SEM expresses that error in raw-score units. Neither reliability nor the reference interval is a diagnosis or a forecast.
psychometrics.brokenLink: This link's result couldn't be read.
psychometrics.jungianPreviewNote: A provisional position that moves as you answer

jungian.metaDescription: Re-read IPIP-50 Big Five responses on the four axes E–I · S–N · T–F · J–P and summarize them as one of 16 MBTI types.
jungian.kicker: MBTI TYPE TEST · BUILT ON IPIP-50
jungian.heroBody: Your completed IPIP-50 Big Five responses are re-read as four continuous axes following the correlation structure reported in comparison literature (McCrae & Costa, 1989), then summarized as one of 16 MBTI type codes. A type is a starting point for self-reflection, not a verdict.
jungian.axesTitle: Follow the gradient, not a border
jungian.axesBody: The poles are different directions, not ranks. When a score is near the center, the letter stays ? instead of forcing a categorical claim onto a continuous response.
jungian.methodTitle: A type is a summary, not a verdict
jungian.methodBody: This screen does not measure a new construct. It linearly re-expresses existing IPIP-50 factor scores. Continuous scores are primary; the four-letter code is a compact format for sharing and remembering. It is not the official MBTI® assessment and has no affiliation with The Myers & Briggs Foundation or the trademark holder.
jungian.sourceMethod: The axis correspondences refer to NEO-PI self-report comparisons reported by McCrae and Costa (1989), not to a user's personal correlation or a new norm. Critiques by Pittenger (1993) and Stein & Swan (2019) are included so the limits of type theory remain visible.
jungian.trademarkNotice: MBTI is a registered trademark of The Myers & Briggs Foundation; this service is not an official MBTI® assessment. This result reinterprets IPIP-50 responses into four axes and a 16-type code using correlation structure described in academic literature.
jungian.resultMetaDescription: An MBTI-style type code with four continuous axis scores derived from IPIP-50 responses.
jungian.resultHero: {code} summarizes your current response pattern. The per-type nickname and profile below are prompts for self-reflection, not a verdict.
jungian.certaintyLabel: Reference certainty at the least decisive axis: {percent}%
jungian.axisBoundaryNotice: This axis is close to its midpoint, so no letter was forced. Read both poles as observation prompts, not as a ranking.
jungian.boundaryNote: ? does not mean the result is incomplete. It is a guardrail against using an arbitrary cut point to overstate a continuous response pattern.
jungian.typeImageAlt: A self-reflection illustration for the {code} type
jungian.typeImageNote: Use this image as a flexible visual prompt, not as a fixed identity.
jungian.boundaryTypeSummary: At least one axis is close to the midpoint, so the full code remains open.
jungian.boundaryTypeDetail: Start with the continuous positions of all four axes. If a result changes, the item responses and present context may have changed; that alone is not evidence that your personality changed.
jungian.openBigFiveResult: Return to the Big Five result

darktriad.metaDescription: Measure Machiavellianism, Narcissism, and Psychopathy using the 27-item Short Dark Triad (SD3).
darktriad.heroTitle: Exploring the darker side of personality
darktriad.heroBody: Uses the Short Dark Triad scale by Jones & Paulhus (2014). Answer 27 questions to see continuous scores and normative positions for three traits. High scores don't mean you're a bad person—they show the direction and strength of these characteristics.
darktriad.scaleNote: Scores range from 9 to 45. Norms are based on 17,682 responses from OpenPsychometrics.org. High scores are not a diagnosis or prediction.
darktriad.reliabilityNote: Internal consistency (Cronbach α): Machiavellianism 0.77, Narcissism 0.74, Psychopathy 0.77.
darktriad.resultMetaDescription: Machiavellianism, Narcissism, and Psychopathy results calculated from SD3 27-item responses.
darktriad.unansweredWarning: {n} items still unanswered. Answer all to see your results.
darktriad.midpointCaution: Midpoint response rate is {rate}%. Results may be unstable due to many undecided items.

horoscope.heroBody: The day changes over at your own local midnight. Nothing is stored on a server — it's calculated fresh, right there.
horoscope.emptyBody: No birth info has been entered yet.
horoscope.metaDescription: Pick a zodiac sign or a zodiac animal to see a short glimpse of today.

horoscopeReading.evidenceCaption: The selected lines are tied to these calculated observations.
horoscopeReading.evidenceSelectionNote: For each slot, the signal with the highest calculated slot score was selected. Relevance weights are editorial placement rules, not predictive probabilities.
horoscopeReading.personalizeTitle: Use your birth profile for a deeper view
horoscopeReading.personalizeBody: The public reading uses sign-level observations. A saved profile can open the private calculation route without sending your birth data to a server.
horoscopeReading.noteUtcNoonReference: The public page uses UTC noon because it does not know the visitor's location.
horoscopeReading.noteWholeSignPrecision: Public sign-page relationships use whole-sign precision in 30-degree sectors.
horoscopeReading.noteDegreeTransitPrecision: The private page also considers degree-based aspects between natal and current planets.
horoscopeReading.noteCulturalTier: The calculation rules are fixed, but the predictive effect of the interpretation has not been empirically verified; it remains a cultural reference.

psychometricsDeep.midpointCaution: Midpoint responses make up {rate}% of this factor. Read its direction cautiously and observe your behavior across other situations.
psychometricsDeep.itemStrongTitle: Responses scored high in this factor's direction
psychometricsDeep.itemWeakTitle: Responses scored low in this factor's direction
psychometricsDeep.normSource: Norm sample: {n} respondents from the Open Source Psychometrics Project IPIP data
psychometricsDeep.normScope: An English-language online public sample; no age- or gender-specific norm is used.
psychometricsDeep.normUnavailable: No comparable norm data is available for this factor.
psychometricsDeep.retestKicker: Previous result stored only in this browser
psychometricsDeep.retestTitle: Compare this result with the last one
psychometricsDeep.retestBody: The cards show raw-score differences from your previous test ({date}). Changes can reflect context, response framing, and measurement error.
psychometricsDeep.retestNoChange: All five raw scores were the same this time. Treat a stable result as a reference point for the present context, not a fixed label.
psychometricsDeep.retestCaution: A change does not prove that your personality changed. A longer interval and notes about real behavior provide a more balanced comparison.

referencesPage.title: Sources behind calculation and interpretation
referencesPage.intro: The libraries used for calculation and the historical references for each tradition are listed by feature. A source does not mean that a cultural interpretation has verified predictive power.
referencesPage.jungian: MBTI type test · Big Five re-expression
referencesPage.horoscope: Daily reading · sky and day-pillar calculation
referencesPage.note: The relevant references are repeated inside detailed result blocks. Sources with URLs can be opened in the original publication or repository.

glossaryPage.title: Glossary
glossaryPage.intro: Short explanations for technical terms used in calculated values and interpretations. The evidence tier is kept visible so definitions are not mistaken for validated predictions.

evidenceRef.definition: An internal link from an interpretation sentence to the calculation value it uses. It does not automatically prove the interpretation true, but broken links can be tested.

tenGod.definition: Traditional Saju vocabulary that expresses the Five-Element and polarity relationship between the Day Master and another character through ten roles.

growthStage.definition: Traditional Saju vocabulary that reads the relationship between a Day Master's stem and a branch through a twelve-stage life-cycle metaphor. Illness and Death are not medical or lifespan predictions.

trueSolar.definition: A time value adjusted from standard clock time by birthplace longitude and the equation of time to approximate the Sun's apparent position.

house.definition: A symbolic sector in an astrology chart, dividing the zodiac into twelve areas from the Ascendant and birthplace.

aspect.definition: A calculated relationship that checks whether the ecliptic separation between two bodies is close to a reference angle such as conjunction, square, or trine.

tScore.definition: A standardized score based on a norm sample's mean and standard deviation. LUMINA uses a mean of 50 and standard deviation of 10.

percentile.definition: A 1–99 position showing where a raw response score falls in the reference distribution. It is not a Korean population norm.

sem.definition: An estimate of how much a score may vary across repeated measurement of the same trait, based on reliability and standard deviation.

masterNumber.definition: A numerology rule that keeps 11, 22, and 33 as distinct symbols instead of reducing them to one digit.

jungianAxis.definition: Test axes that re-express Big Five Extraversion, Openness, Agreeableness, and Conscientiousness scores — with no new items — as the four continuous directions E–I · S–N · T–F · J–P and summarize them into a 16-type code.

typeBoundary.definition: A marker used when an axis is close to its midpoint, so an arbitrary letter is not forced. It preserves continuity rather than indicating a missing result.

methodologyPage.title: Public validation methodology
methodologyPage.intro: The fixed test criteria and limitations are shown together so users can inspect the quality evidence behind each calculation engine.
methodologyPage.sajuCases: Saju: all four pillars matched the independent lunar-javascript oracle in 436 cases
methodologyPage.astroCases: Astrology: 200 comparisons across 20 charts plus 803 five-day samples from 2020–2030 × 10 bodies = 8,030 comparisons against astronomia (VSOP87/Meeus lineage), all under 0.05°
methodologyPage.dayCases: Daily pillar: all 73,414 days from 1900-01-01 through 2100-12-31 matched lunar-javascript with zero mismatches
methodologyPage.norms: Big Five: aggregate norms built from 551,607 quality-filtered rows out of 1,015,341 public IPIP records
methodologyPage.determinism: Tarot and numerology: deterministic reproducibility tests for seeded shuffle and digit/letter-value arithmetic
methodologyPage.jungian: MBTI type test: unit tests fix the linear re-expression of existing IPIP-50 scores, four axis directions, boundary behavior, 16 type profiles, and their literature basis
methodologyPage.limitsBody: Saju, astrology, tarot, and numerology use calculated inputs, but their symbolic sentences do not provide empirical validation that future events can be predicted. The Big Five norm is also an English-language online public sample, not a Korean population norm.
methodologyPage.notYet: The 8,030 astrology comparisons use a five-day grid, so they do not guarantee an exhaustive error check for every instant. The Big Five norm is an English-language public sample without age- or gender-stratified norms.

policy.draftNote: Effective 2026-08-18 · This document is a draft and requires legal review before publishing.
policy.privacy1Body: LUMINA works without sign-up or login. We don't collect identifying information like a name, email, or phone number, and no account table exists at all. Inputs like birth date and birthplace are used only for that moment's calculation and are never stored per-person on a server.
policy.privacy2Title: 2. What you enter stays only in this browser
policy.privacy2Body: Your birth info is saved to this browser's localStorage so you don't have to re-enter it. This value is never sent to a server and never leaves this device's browser. You can delete it completely at any time with "Clear My Info" on the input screen.
policy.privacy3Body: When you share a result, your inputs are compressed and embedded directly in the link's address. Anyone who opens that link can recompute the same result (without going through a server). Since no result is stored on a server, deleting the link removes any way to access that result. Identifying information like a name is never included in the link to begin with.
policy.privacy4Body: Your 50 question responses also aren't stored on a server. They're embedded in the result address, and the score is simply calculated on the spot from that.
policy.privacy5Body: If palm-reading analysis is added in the future, our principle is that images are processed on-device only and are never transmitted to or stored on a server.
policy.privacy6Body: Google AdSense ads may be shown to support operating the service. If you decline ad consent, non-personalized ads are shown instead. How Google and other ad partners handle information collected via cookies or device identifiers follows each company's own privacy policy.
policy.privacy7Body: For security and incident response, our web server and hosting infrastructure may retain standard access logs (IP address, request time, request path, etc.) for a limited period. These logs are not linked to any individual profile.
policy.privacy8Body: For questions about this policy, please use the contact details listed within the service.
policy.terms1Body: LUMINA is a self-reflection and entertainment service that combines traditional interpretive systems — Saju, astrology, tarot, numerology — with publicly available academic scales like IPIP-50. Every result screen shows which evidence tier it belongs to (scientifically verified, cultural interpretation, or entertainment).
policy.terms2Title: 2. Not medical, legal, or financial advice
policy.terms2Body: No result may be used as a basis for medical diagnosis, legal counsel, or investment decisions. For decisions involving your health, legal matters, or finances, always consult a qualified professional in that field.
policy.terms3Title: 3. Basis and limits of the calculations
policy.terms3Body: The Saju and astrology calculations (solar terms, planetary positions, true solar time correction, etc.) are based on verifiable astronomical and calendrical data. However, the claim that how these results fall predicts life events has not been scientifically verified. Tarot and numerology follow fixed rules (shuffle algorithms, letter-value arithmetic, etc.) but are likewise not predictive tools.
policy.terms4Body: We maintain a content policy against language that induces fear or states things as deterministic fact. Even so, use under a guardian's guidance is recommended.
policy.terms5Body: Because there are no accounts, we don't apply sanctions (suspension, blocking, etc.) based on user identification. That said, automated bulk requests that threaten service stability may be limited at the infrastructure level.
policy.terms6Body: The service is provided as-is, and we do not guarantee the complete accuracy of calculation results or continuous availability. Our liability for damages arising from use of the service is limited to the extent permitted by law.
policy.terms7Body: When features are added or policies change, this page is updated along with its effective date.

attachment.title: Attachment Style Test
attachment.description: Discover your attachment style (secure, anxious, avoidant, fearful) with 36 ECR-R questions.
attachment.heroDescription: Discover the patterns you show in intimate relationships. We analyze your attachment style along two dimensions: anxiety and avoidance.
attachment.aboutTitle: What is an attachment style test?
attachment.aboutDescription: Attachment theory explains how early relationships with caregivers influence patterns in adult intimate relationships. This test is based on Brennan, Clark & Shaver's (1998) Experiences in Close Relationships-Revised (ECR-R) scale and measures two dimensions: anxiety (worry about abandonment) and avoidance (discomfort with closeness).
attachment.footerNote1: ※ This test is a tool for self-reflection and does not replace clinical diagnosis.
attachment.footerNote2: ※ Results are stored only in this browser and are never sent to a server.
attachment.resultDescription: Results from the ECR-R based attachment style test.
attachment.errorMessage: The link is invalid or the data is corrupted. Please start the test again.
attachment.interpretationP1: Attachment style is not a fixed trait but can change with relationship experiences. There is a tendency to move toward secure attachment as you experience safe relationships.
attachment.interpretationP2: Anxious and avoidant styles are 'insecure' but this is not a pathological diagnosis. However, recognizing which patterns repeat in relationships is the first step toward change.
attachment.interpretationP3: Fearful attachment (disorganized) involves high anxiety and high avoidance, and professional counseling may be helpful.
attachment.scienceP1: The ECR-R is one of the most widely used self-report measures of adult attachment. Developed by Fraley, Waller & Brennan (2000), it shows high internal consistency for both anxiety (α=0.91) and avoidance (α=0.93).
attachment.scienceP2: The four-category model (Bartholomew & Horowitz, 1991) classifies attachment into secure, anxious, avoidant, and fearful based on combinations of anxiety and avoidance.
attachment.scienceP3: Normative data uses estimates from Fraley's (2000) meta-analysis. Anxiety mean 2.92 (SD=1.22), avoidance mean 2.68 (SD=1.18).
